messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Design request. Has to land softer than 6 m/s. The motor mount is 18 mm. Can you design something that reaches about 250 m? We launch off a 1 m rod. Provide the design and expected performance.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: about 250 m, landing softer than 6 m/s, an 18 mm motor mount, and a 1 m launch rod. No wind is stated, so 2 m/s is the default. The 1 m rod has to be passed on every flight.
2. Feasibility: about 250 m is a 5% band, 238 to 262 m. An 18 mm mount takes an 18 mm motor, so 24 mm Estes motors are out. Vacuum speed is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 250) = 70.0 m/s. With drag, a C-class motor near 10 N*s is the right size; a B may fall short. The 1 m rod needs a light rocket so rail exit stays above 15 m/s. Looking up C6 and B6.

2. Feasibility: the B6 is 4.3 N*s and the only delay is 0 s, so it is both short on impulse and plugged. The Estes C6 is 8.8 N*s at 4.8 N average, 18 mm, 0.07 m long, 0.0231 kg, with 3, 5 and 7 s delays. It fits the 18 mm mount. Average thrust is only 4.8 N, so on a 1 m rod the rocket has to stay near 40 g or the exit speed drops under 15 m/s. I will use the 5 s delay.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.038 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 4.8 / (0.038 * 9.81) = 12.9. Pad weight 0.038 * 9.81 = 0.373 N, rail acceleration (4.8 - 0.373) / 0.038 = 117 m/s^2, exit speed on the 1 m rod sqrt(2 * 117 * 1) = 15.3 m/s. Propellant is 0.011 kg, descent mass 0.038 - 0.011 = 0.027 kg. At 5 m/s, under 6 m/s, area = 2 * 0.027 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 5^2) = 0.0216 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.0216 / 3.1416) = 0.166 m. I will use 0.30 m so the landing stays soft even if the rocket is a little heavier. Burn is 1.83 s, so the 5 s delay ejects near 6.8 s.
4. Draft: a light 22 mm cardboard rocket. Nose 0.05 m ogive polystyrene. Tube 0.22 m, outer diameter 0.022 m, wall 0.4 mm. Mount 0.019 m outside, 0.08 m long, wall 0.4 mm, Estes C6 with a 5 s delay. Three balsa fins, root 0.045 m, tip 0.018 m, span 0.028 m, sweep 0.018 m, 2 mm thick. One 0.30 m polyethylene chute on ejection. Simulating on a 1 m rod.

messages.reasoning_content:
4. Check: the flight did not run. The tool rejected the design because the chute material was plain polyethylene, which is not an allowed surface material.
5. Fix: the failing item is the chute material. I am changing it to polyethylene (thin). The airframe, C6-5, fins and the 1 m rod stay the same.

4. Check: too high and unstable, and the rod is fine. The simulator gives 457.9 m. (457.9 - 250) / 250 = 0.83, well outside the 5% band. The 5% band is 238 to 262 m. Margin is 0.21 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Landing is 2.7 m/s, under 6 m/s. Rail exit on the 1 m rod is 22.5 m/s, thrust-to-weight 13.5. Mass is only 0.0363 kg, which is why a C6 went so high: the 22 mm tube has very little drag. The chute opens at 6.9 s, just before the 7.17 s apogee, at 9.7 m/s.
5. Fix: the failing values are 457.9 m and 0.21 cal. I cannot add much mass, because 4.8 N on this rod is already close to the 15 m/s exit once the rocket gets heavier. Drag has to come from a wider tube and from fins that are actually big enough. New tube: 0.30 m cardboard, outer diameter 0.033 m, wall 0.5 mm. Nose 0.07 m to match. Fins: root 0.090 m, tip 0.035 m, span 0.060 m, sweep 0.040 m, still 2 mm balsa. Same C6-5, same 0.30 m chute, same 1 m rod.

4. Check: closer, still high and still under-stable. The simulator gives 281.4 m, and (281.4 - 250) / 250 = 0.126, above the 262 m edge of the band. Margin is 0.78 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Landing is 3.4 m/s. The 1 m rod exit is 20.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight 9.6, so there is a little room to add mass. The chute opens at 6.9 s, just after the 6.53 s apogee, at 3.0 m/s. Mass is 0.0511 kg.
5. Fix: the failing values are 281.4 m and 0.78 cal. I am enlarging the balsa fins to root 0.11 m, tip 0.040 m, span 0.072 m, sweep 0.048 m, and adding 0.008 kg of clay at the top of the tube. The fin drag and the nose mass both pull the altitude down, and both move the margin up. Motor, chute, tube and the 1 m rod stay.

4. Check: this one sits in the band and the gates pass. The simulator gives 255.8 m, and (255.8 - 250) / 250 = 0.023, inside 5%. Margin is 1.34 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Landing is 3.8 m/s, under 6 m/s. The 1 m rod exit is 19.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight 8.1. The C6 is 18 mm. The chute opens at 6.9 s, just after the 6.54 s apogee, at 2.8 m/s. Mass is 0.0607 kg.
5. Fix: no further change. Altitude, the 18 mm motor, landing speed, the short rod and the stability gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: 255.8 m is near the middle of the band, but the rocket is only 0.0607 kg, so a heavy paint job or a thicker tube will both drop the altitude and slow the 19.7 m/s rod exit. Margin is 1.34 cal. The 5 s delay matches this flight; a 7 s delay would open later and faster. The 3.8 m/s landing assumes the 0.30 m chute is packed.
messages.content:
Estes C6-5 in a 33 mm cardboard rocket with an 18 mm mount, balsa fins, 8 g of nose clay and a 0.30 m chute, launched from a 1 m rod.
Apogee is 255.8 m, about 2% over 250 m and inside the band. Landing is 3.8 m/s, under 6 m/s. Margin is 1.34 cal. Rod exit is 19.7 m/s.
The 5 s delay opens the chute just after apogee at 2.8 m/s.
